chunks: And as for what Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever reaches the Mash'ar al-Haram on the Day of Nahar before the sun's decline has completed the Hajj."

key_terms.الْمَشْعَرَ الْحَرَامَ: The Mash'ar al-Haram, a sacred station in Mina
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: The decline of the sun (solar noon transition)
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Nahar (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the time limit for reaching Mash'ar al-Haram to complete Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the critical timing of the Wuquf at Mash'ar al-Haram, linking it directly to the validity of the Hajj. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on precise adherence to ritual timings, where reaching the station before solar decline (Zawal) on the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah is a decisive condition for a complete pilgrimage.
